features.headline: Untold stories of Detroit Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown's German upbringing
features.desc: For Amon-Ra St. Brown, Sunday's NFL game in Munich will mark the ultimate convergence of his dual heritage. Here are stories that shed more light.
body: DETROIT — When the Detroit Lions take the field to face the New England Patriots at Allianz Arena in Munich on Sunday, wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown will feel right at home.
For St. Brown, Germany is as much his home as the United States. It's where he and his family frequently took trips to visit his maternal grandparents.

It's where St. Brown went to preschool (Die Rheinpiraten Kindergarten, to be exact), and where he and his older brothers, Equanimeous and Osiris, spent countless hours on bike tours and fishing trips with their grandfather, Helmut Steyer, who enjoyed entertaining his American-born grandsons.

It's where Amon-Ra (and Osiris) was a standout for the country's under-19 national football team. It's where he has hosted football camps since becoming a pro in 2021. And it's where the Lions star was once asked by an uncle to stay in order to become a star in the other type of football.
"It's not strange to him. It's all familiar... everything," St. Brown's mother, Miriam Brown, said. "Going to restaurants, everything is different but for him it's familiar."

The deep connection and familiarity St. Brown has with the country is because of Miriam. Born and raised in Leverkusen, in western Germany, she instilled her German values into Amon-Ra and his brothers, who are all fluent in German.

Those values, and experiences, are a part of St. Brown's identity and have always been at the forefront of who he is. As a result, when the Lions face the Patriots in one of the country's most famous arenas (9:30 a.m. ET on Fox), St. Brown will be the headline act.

features.headline: Patriots are 6-0 after a regular-season loss under Vrabel: Can they do it again?
features.desc: The Patriots play in Munich, Germany, this week. Catch up on what's happening abroad in this week's Patriots notebook,
body: MUNICH — Quick-hit thoughts and notes around the New England Patriots and NFL:

1. Patriots resolve: The Patriots are 6-0 under coach Mike Vrabel in regular-season games after a loss, and they look to keep that streak alive Sunday as underdogs against the Detroit Lions at FC Bayern Munich Arena (Fox, 9:30 a.m. ET).

Quarterback Drake Maye summed up Vrabel's knack for bringing out the best in his team in those situations, saying, "Coach Vrabes always says, 'Try not to ride the roller coaster. Try to ride the merry-go-round.' Keep going around and trying to keep the same mindset."

A seven-hour international trip to Munich after the sting of last week's 45-27 home loss to the Packers has created a unique challenge. Not to mention the 6-2 Lions are among the league's upper-echelon teams, playing in arguably the league's best division, the NFC North.

The 5-4 Patriots have their bye after the game, but the urgency around the team has been evident as it tries to stay afloat in the AFC playoff chase. If the playoffs started today, the Patriots would be the No. 7 and final seed in the AFC.
Starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson, who has a knee tendon issue that is threatening his availability for the game, has been pushing to play.
Likewise with receiver A.J. Brown, who missed the past two games because of a knee flare-up but returned to practice this week and had Vrabel feeling "pretty good" about his status early Friday.

As for the defense, which was carved up by the Packers in an uncharacteristic string of fundamental and communication breakdowns, the unit struck Vrabel's merry-go-round theme with its approach this week.

features.headline: Falcons insist winning still the goal despite trading Jessie Bates III
features.desc: Atlanta wanted to ensure trading away Jessie Bates III didn't send the wrong message to the team.
body: FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — Overcommunication. That has been the order of business over the past several days for Atlanta Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski.
That has included one-on-one meetings with players, small-group conversations with the team's player leadership committee and full team meetings.
Stefanski has wanted to make it absolutely certain that the Falcons, despite trading two starters before the NFL trade deadline earlier this week, are not in any way giving up on this season.

"I would tell you we've got a great group of leadership on this team," Stefanski said. "I've talked to them a lot over the last few days — like I do all the time, but in particular now. I'm very, very confident in their leadership."

On Monday, the Falcons traded All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Bates, aside from being arguably the best safety in the league, was also a team captain and one of the most respected veterans in the building.

A day later, Atlanta traded starting center Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens for reserve guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick. Neuzil was a Falcons success story, starting with the team as an undrafted free agent and working his way up to a starting role.

The Falcons are 3-6. So, in that respect, it made perfect sense to get value back for two players who were set to become free agents in the offseason. With regards to Bates, a safety had not been acquired for a second-round pick since 2018. Few could blame Atlanta for making the move.

features.headline: Despite Cousins trade, are Vikings back to square one at QB?
features.desc: Cousins can give some short-term relief, but his future and the search for a franchise QB remain uncertain.
body: EAGAN, Minn. — The Minnesota Vikings drew external praise and generated internal celebration this week after reacquiring quarterback Kirk Cousins, a beloved figure among team employees and a player with at least a reasonable chance of stabilizing an offense that has flopped in the past two seasons.
Regardless of how the next few months play out, however, the trade guarantees the Vikings will be in a familiar place next spring: looking for a starting quarterback.
There is a conceivable path toward keeping Cousins in 2027, but it wouldn't be simple — and that's assuming he wants to play a 16th NFL season at age 39.
Cousins' contract contains three void years from 2027 to 2029, giving the Vikings two options: Pay a $10 million roster bonus and bid him farewell, or negotiate a new contract.
Anyone familiar with Cousins' business acumen knows that if he were to do anything other than demand a premium quarterback deal, it would be the first time in his career.

The topic surfaced briefly amid the week's chaos. General manager Nolan Teasley said there is "always potential" for exploring a future with Cousins, adding that the Vikings "understood everything that we were inheriting."
Teasley was referencing Cousins' contract, but in a larger sense, it has always been clear that the GM inherited a perpetually open-ended quarterback situation when the Vikings hired him May 30.

The decision to sign Kyler Murray to a one-year contract two months before Teasley arrived signaled the termination of the organization's faith in 2024 first-round pick J.J. McCarthy, who was traded away in September.

features.headline: Why the Raiders named Fernando Mendoza as the starter
features.desc: The Raiders named Fernando Mendoza as the starter shortly after trading Kirk Cousins to the Vikings.
body: HENDERSON, Nev. — There isn't a particular moment that convinced the Las Vegas Raiders players and coaches that No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza was ready to be the team's starting quarterback. It's a collection of things the rookie has done since he arrived at the facility in April.
For coach Klint Kubiak, it's Mendoza's improvement in his accuracy and knowledge of the offense each week.

A month ago, backup quarterback Aidan O'Connell recalled watching Mendoza make a few throws in practice, causing him to turn to quarterbacks coach Mike Sullivan and assistant head coach Mike McCoy and say, "Those were incredible."

Wide receiver Tre Tucker, on the other hand, knew Mendoza was capable of being QB1 when he watched the College Football Playoff National Championship game this past January and saw him lower his shoulder to knock off a Miami defender before diving into the end zone for a touchdown that helped Indiana secure its first-ever title.
"That shows you the kind of guy we are getting," Tucker said.

On Tuesday, Mendoza was named the starting quarterback after the Raiders traded veteran Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings. The Raiders' decision to move on from Cousins sent shock waves through the locker room.
But with Mendoza, the first quarterback taken by the Raiders in the first round since 2007, waiting in the wings, the team knew this moment would come at some point.

As abrupt as the change of power might have felt, the Raiders believe Mendoza is ready for his starting debut Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks, the reigning Super Bowl champs and one of the league's most menacing defenses.

features.headline: Wake Forest claims 'Bachelor U' status after Sam Hartman news
features.desc: Wake Forest football is the only program, the school says, to have had three former players feature in "The Bachelor" franchise.
body: On Friday, the football-watching world was rocked with news from an unlikely source: "The Bachelor."

The reality TV dating show announced its Season 30 lead would be Sam Hartman — a Washington Commanders quarterback who, before joining the professional ranks, spent five seasons at Wake Forest and one at Notre Dame.
Now, the Demon Deacons are using Hartman's television stardom turn as an opportunity to lay claim to an unusual but distinctive claim: "Bachelor U."

The former All-ACC signal-caller isn't the first Wake Forest football alumnus to take his talents to the show. In fact, he's not even the second, leading the Demon Deacons to stamp their latest superlative: "Only school in the nation with three former players in the Bachelor franchise."

Other former Demon Deacons who were featured in the franchise include Matt James (Season 25 of "The Bachelor") and Tyler Cameron (Season 15 of "The Bachelorette"). James was a wide receiver in Winston-Salem from 2011 to 2014, and Cameron served as a backup quarterback from 2012 to 2014.

The new accolade is just another feather in the cap for Wake Forest football in a heady time for the program. The 8-1 Demon Deacons are No. 13 in the College Football Playoff rankings and just inked head coach Jake Dickert to a new contract extension on Thursday.
